body:
incident-bot: INCIDENT — P95 latency spike detected on inference-hostpool-prod-1. Alert threshold breached, paging oncall.

sasha: Acked. Investigating. Observed p95 ~ 760ms (baseline ~200ms). p50 ~ 120ms.

jordan: Seeing same on dashboards (us-west-2). Multiple customers impacted, high-QPS models. No 5xx, just slow.

mike: Pulled traces: tail shows majority of time in decoder attention kernel (attention_cuda_kernel) during generation. span breakdown: model_token_decode -> attention_kernel ~ 85% of token time.

tess: Any recent infra or runtime deploys? eng-releases shows a rolling kernel image bump started 2026-03-15 09:02 UTC (kernel 5.19.15 -> 5.19.18) on many nodes.

eli: Confirm — infra scheduled a micro-upgrade overnight; roll started at 09:02 UTC, one-third of pool updated so far.

sasha: Hypothesis: kernel micro-upgrade changed scheduler or driver interaction, impacting CPU->GPU transfer latency. Need perf counters, dmesg, and nv driver logs from hot nodes.

jordan: SSHing to a hot node to grab perf and `nvidia-smi --query` logs now.

mike: Paste from traces: 
```
TRACE SUMMARY (sample):
model_token_decode: 320ms
 -> attention_kernel: 260ms
 -> softmax: 20ms
 -> matmul: 30ms
```

jordan: Quick `perf stat -e cycles,instructions,cache-misses,context-switches -p <pid>` on generator shows context-switches jumped 10x during spike window.

sasha: Context-switch increase suggests CPU-side scheduling interference that can hurt the data feeding pipeline to GPU.

tess: Any kernel logs (dmesg/syslog) showing panics or driver warnings?

eli: dmesg snippet from an affected node: 
```
Mar 15 09:05:12 kernel: watchdog: task kworker/2:3 blocked for 125 secs
Mar 15 09:05:12 kernel: INFO: task kworker/2:3: ... Tainted: G W
```

mike: Also saw `perf top` showing heavy samples in `throttled_copy()` in our nvlink transfer layer during the spike.

jordan: Quick mitigation applied: pinned hot model routes to nodes that are not yet upgraded and scaled the dedicated pool +30%.

sasha: Executed pinning and scaling. After ~6 minutes p95 improved to ~230ms. :tada:

tess: Good. For the post-incident RCA we need:
- full perf samples (affected and unaffected nodes)
- flamegraphs for token-decode path
- kernel versions and package diffs per node
- list of infra changes/deployments in the window
- full traces for range of affected trace ids (attach examples)

mike: Uploaded perf tarball to incident artifacts: s3://redwood-incidents/1836004321/perf.tar.gz

jordan: Timeline draft:
- 09:02 UTC: kernel rolling upgrade started
- 09:05 UTC: p95 began rising sharply
- 09:12 UTC: mitigation: pin hot models to pre-upgrade nodes
- 09:18 UTC: p95 reduced to ~230ms
- 09:22 UTC: pool scaled +30%

eli: Customer impact: ~7% of requests experienced >500ms latency for ~15 minutes. Top QPS customers saw degraded UX, no request failures.

sasha: Handoff to night oncall (tess) for monitoring and RCA lead. Handoff notes:
- Mitigations: pinning + scaling in place
- Artifacts: perf tarball, dmesg, traces uploaded
- Next steps: reproduce kernel bump in staging, run microbench with kernel 5.19.18, collect perf/flamegraphs

tess: Acked, taking RCA lead. I'll coordinate with infra/kernel team tomorrow. Creating tracking issue: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-1836004321

incident-bot: Incident status updated -> mitigated. Please populate root_cause within 48h and attach final analysis.

sasha: Quick root-cause hypotheses to track in RCA thread:
1) Kernel micro-upgrade changed scheduler/timer behavior, increasing context-switches on kworkers that affect GPU transfer latency.
2) New kernel+nv driver interaction hits `throttled_copy()` path more often, causing longer NV transfer prep times.
3) Increased CPU preemption decreased effective batching efficiency, raising per-token latency.

mike: I'll generate flamegraphs and a perf report; tagging @infra-kernel and @gpu-driver teams for kernel/driver symbol correlation.

jordan: I'll export p50/p95 CSVs and attach to the Jira.

eli: Draft customer comms: short status, mitigation summary, apology, and promise of RCA in 48-72h.

sasha: Thanks everyone. Closing active thread — keep logs and artifacts retained for 90 days. :lock:
